00C1.name: Slot minus one of sprite state
desc: Only real use: Yoshi runs away after Mario is hit by a smoke puff ($02:A488 `STA $C1,X`, value 2). X is [$18DF]
(Yoshi slot plus one), so this probably lands on Yoshi's own $00C2 state entry.
All other hits are the byte $C1 inside pointer tables (growing vine, Chuck states, scroll routines).
Values: 2 = Yoshi state 'runs away'.

00C2.name: Sprite state
00C2.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: General-purpose state number of each sprite slot, the 'which phase am I in' variable of the sprite's main routine.
Most sprites dispatch through a pointer table on it and advance it with INC (State++) or reset it with STZ.
Meaning is per sprite type: Urchin and Big Boo phases, Wall springboard compression (signed), Turn block bridge
0 = extending / 1 = retracting, Flying question block (wings fall off), Power-up 'clear when free'.
Slot 0 is $00C2, slot 1 is $00C3, ... slot 11 is $00CD.
Values: 0 = initial / idle state; higher values = later phases (sprite specific).

00CB.name: Bonus game flag
desc: Set to 1 by the Init bonus game sprite ($01:DE08 `LDA #$01 : STA $CB`). No sample reads it back directly, so it
is probably a leftover flag. As sprite slot 9 state it is also the $00C2 table element (see $00C2).
Other hits are the byte $CB inside pointers (level data, cutscene state tables).
Values: 1 = set by bonus game init.

00CE.name: Sprite data pointer, low byte
desc: Low byte of the long pointer to the current level's sprite list. Load Level copies the pointer from Ptrs05EC00 into
$00CE/$00CF and forces the bank byte $00D0 to $07; it then reads the list header with `LDA [$CE]`.
Spawn-sprite-from-level-data and the Sprite list loop walk it with `LDA [$CE],Y` (format YYYYEEsy per entry in
horizontal levels). Chocolate Island 2 also rewrites it from its own sprite table.
Other hits are the byte $CE inside pointer words.

00CF.name: Sprite data pointer, high byte
desc: High byte of the 16-bit address within bank $07 of the level's sprite list. Set with `STA $CF` in Load level
($05:D8F3) from the second byte of the pointer table entry; read together with $00CE through `[$CE]`.
Other hits are the byte $CF inside pointer words (cutscene states, Koopa Kid states, level tally).

00D0.name: Sprite data pointer, bank byte
desc: Bank byte of the sprite list pointer. Load level sets it to $07 because all level sprite data lives in bank $07.
Hits at $05:C6A8 are misdisassembled data (a TRB that is really other code), not a real use.
Values: $07 = sprite data bank.

00D1.name: Mario X position copy, low
desc: Copy of Mario's X position, low byte ([$94] is the original). Game mode 14 (in level, $00:A2F7) copies $0094 into
$00D1 each frame, in 16-bit mode, so $00D2 receives the high byte. Sprite routines use it as Mario's position
(Mario horizontal position relative to sprite, Release carried sprite, Lakitu's cloud). Lakitu's cloud copies it
into the cloud's X low.
Other hits are the byte $D1 inside pointer words.

00D2.name: Mario X position copy, high
desc: High byte of the copy of Mario's X position ([$95] is the original), filled together with $00D1 from game mode 14.
Read by Mario horizontal position relative to sprite, Release carried sprite and Lakitu's cloud logic.
Other hits are the byte $D2 inside pointer words (cutscene states, Mario animation routines).

00D3.name: Mario Y position copy, low
desc: Copy of Mario's Y position, low byte ([$96] is the original), written each frame from game mode 14 ($00:A2FB).
Used by sprites as Mario's Y: sprite-minus-Mario distance for stomp/bounce, Lakitu's cloud
(cloud Y = Mario Y + offset), pipe animation. Boo main routine temporarily subtracts [$18B6] from it to aim above Mario's feet, then restores it.

00D4.name: Mario Y position copy, high
desc: High byte of the copy of Mario's Y position ([$97] is the original), filled with $00D3 from game mode 14.
Read by the stomp/hurt contact check, position-relative routines and Lakitu; Boo main routine also writes it
while aiming. Put Mario on Yoshi copies a value into it. Other hits are the byte $D4 inside pointer words.

00D5.name: Wiggler buffer pointer, low
desc: Low byte of a temporary long pointer to a Wiggler's position history buffer ([$D5],Y). Wiggler init and main
routine store the sprite's X/Y low into the buffer through it; Wiggler draw reads each segment's history back.
Set from sprite slot n AND 3 plus $7B at $02:F011. Other hits are the byte $D5 inside level data pointers.

00D6.name: Wiggler buffer pointer, middle
desc: High byte of the Wiggler buffer address: $9A plus a per-slot offset (DATA_02EFEE). Set at $02:F022 by Wiggler
init. With $00D7 = $7F the buffer is at $7F:9A7B + n * $80 (n = slot AND 3). Other hits are the byte $D6 inside
pointer tables (sprite init/main routines, level data).

00D7.name: Wiggler buffer pointer, bank
desc: Bank byte of the Wiggler buffer pointer; Wiggler init sets it to $7F. Other hits are the byte $D7 inside pointer
tables (line-guide platform routines, Chocolate Island 2 sprite table, level data).
Values: $7F = Wiggler history buffer bank.

00D8.name: Sprite Y position low
00D8.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Low byte of each sprite's Y position in the level (RAM_SpriteYLo); [$14D4] is the high byte. Everything that
moves a sprite adds speed to it; collision, drawing and block interaction read it.
Slot 0 is $00D8, slot 1 is $00D9, ... slot 11 is $00E3.

00E0.name: Sprite Y position low, slot 8
desc: Y low of sprite slot 8. Bowser's Mechakoopa drop and ball throw (and phase 9 bounce) write it directly to place
a newly spawned sprite below Bowser: Bowser Y low + $40 (or +$47), then InitSpriteTables with X = 8.
Other hits are the byte $E0 inside pointers (Fireball init/main, level data).

00E4.name: Sprite X position low
00E4.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Low byte of each sprite's X position in the level (RAM_SpriteXLo); [$14E0] is the high byte. Moved by speed,
read by collision, drawing and block interaction, and by Mario-relative checks.
Slot 0 is $00E4, slot 1 is $00E5, ... slot 11 is $00EF.

00EC.name: Sprite X position low, slot 8
desc: X low of sprite slot 8. Bowser's Mechakoopa drop/ball throw and phase 9 bounce write it directly: Bowser X low + 8,
to place the new sprite, then InitSpriteTables with X = 8. Other hits are the byte $EC inside pointer tables
(Chocolate Island 2 layer 1 data, overworld event states).
